extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing short stories (roughly 1,000–7,000 words) that achieve thematic unity, tight character focus, strong pacing, and polished prose. Emphasizes economy of elements, a single primary conflict, and disciplined revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length (word count) and scale
rubrics_metrics.description: 1,000–7,000 words; 2–3 characters; 'a single powerful message or theme.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short stories should fall roughly in the 1,000–7,000 word range and maintain a compact scale — only a few characters and a focused scope. Because of the shorter format, every element must work harder than in longer formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of elements / every element matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Every element must work harder than in longer formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim anything that doesn't propel plot, character, or theme. Use scenes, details, and sentences that serve multiple purposes rather than padding or extraneous subplots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character count and focus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the cast so the story can develop characters meaningfully within a short span. Avoid introducing unnecessary people who dilute emotional and thematic focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization by implication
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterization should be almost entirely implied. A single detail (e.g., $5 tip on a $10 ride) can convey generosity, privilege, and naïveté simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer showing over telling: choose concrete, multipurpose details that reveal character indirectly. Use actions, objects, and small gestures to suggest backstory and personality instead of explicit exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary conflict concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: One primary conflict, often internal with external manifestations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center the story on a single driving problem or tension. Let external events manifest or complicate the internal struggle, but do not scatter focus across multiple equal conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid subplots
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a short story, subplots reduce intensity and waste limited space. If a subplot doesn't directly illuminate the main conflict or theme, cut it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme: focused exploration and ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore an aspect of human experience thoughtfully. 'You don't have to provide a definitive moral ruling — in fact, it's usually better to keep things ambivalent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to illuminate an idea or experience rather than moralize. Let complexity and ambiguity remain; the story should suggest rather than fully resolve ethical or thematic questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea generation and prompt use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use writing prompts filtered by genre. Popular prompts: running away, obsession, yearning, facing fears, dialogue-only narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with genre-specific prompts to bootstrap concept generation. Consider which prompts naturally lend themselves to compact, focused exploration rather than sprawling plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: POV and structural choices matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider POV and structure carefully — they dramatically affect impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a point of view and structural arrangement that align with the story's thematic focus and emotional perspective. Structural experiments can change what the reader notices and what stays implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening: start late and hook immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: Start 'as close to the end as possible.' Use in medias res, intriguing questions, or vivid imagery to hook immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin near the central action or its immediate lead-up to maximize momentum. Use striking imagery or an immediate problem/question to draw the reader in without prolonged setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternate between significant events and exposition; gradually increase pacing toward climax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the middle to escalate tension: intersperse key scenes with tightly focused exposition, trimming filler. Build momentum so the reader arrives at a clear, intense climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending / natural conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Find the natural conclusion'; end with a standout line; 'drop the mic and get out' — avoid falling action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude when the core question or emotional arc reaches its natural stopping point. Prefer a resonant final sentence or image over extended wrapping-up; avoid over-explaining after the climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision timing: wait before revising
rubrics_metrics.description: Wait days or weeks before revising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time between drafting and revision so you can view the work with fresh eyes. Distance helps identify dead passages, unclear moments, and opportunities to tighten.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene-purpose audit and redundancy elimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine each scene's purpose; eliminate redundancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For every scene ask what it contributes to plot, character, or theme. Remove or combine scenes that repeat information or fail to advance the story's core aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level polish and variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Polish sentence-level prose for variety and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refine wording, rhythm, and sentence length to create momentum and hold reader interest. Use varied sentence structures and strong verbs to heighten clarity and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate mechanical errors (typos, punctuation, formatting) that distract readers or undermine professionalism. Final clean-up ensures the craft choices are what the reader notices.
